X.note: A cut-out portrait with a white outline sits over a shaded-relief map of New York, with an orange dashed route that reads as the Erie Canal. The text block on the right is clean: a gold rule, a clear name/title/date hierarchy, and good contrast against the darkened map. The composition is balanced. The cutout looks like a sticker with no shadow or depth, and the cropped lower body is a little awkward. The source line is small and low contrast. The canal route is unlabeled and split into two disconnected dashed segments, which is slightly ambiguous.

Y.note: A tilted archival photo print on a dark textured background gives a nice tactile feel, and the vintage mood fits the subject. But the caption sits directly over the bottom of the photo, with only a gradient scrim behind it. The white title crosses the pale photo border and the fence, so contrast is weak there. The grey source line is small and low contrast on the fading photo. The photo's subject is small in the frame, there is a large empty dark area at the top and right, and the caption strip cuts into the print. The frame looks unbalanced.

why: X has a clear layout, separated text, strong contrast and added context from the map. Y's caption overlaps the photo and loses contrast, and its subject is small.
top_fix_for_weaker: Move the caption off the photo into a solid or dark panel, for example a lower-third bar or a side column. Enlarge the photo so Hoover fills more of the frame, and raise the source line's size and contrast.
